sections.heading: Why we are writing to you

sentences.text: We are writing because ARX-related neurodevelopmental spectrum and SMC1A-related epileptic encephalopathy are recorded on the same mechanism road: too little protein from loss of function of one copy. [ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:hpoa:OMIM:300215, ev:g2p:G2P02415, ev:hpoa:OMIM:301044]

The recorded phenotype similarity is high, but the shared features are all common, low-information terms, so we should be careful not to over-read that overlap. [ev:rule:simgic, ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:hpoa:OMIM:300215, ev:g2p:G2P02415, ev:hpoa:OMIM:301044]
The gene-disease link is listed as definitive for both ARX and SMC1A. [ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:g2p:G2P02415]
For both conditions, the curated mechanism is loss of function, and this mechanism call is marked as inferred. [ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:g2p:G2P02415]
Both conditions have reported disease models in PubMed. [ev:pubmed:models:ARX, ev:pubmed:models:SMC1A]
No targeted clinical trial was found for either condition in the sources searched. [ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:g2p:G2P02415]
No approved disease-specific therapy was found for either condition in the sources searched. [ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:g2p:G2P02415]

sections.heading: What we would like to learn from or reuse

sentences.text: Registry design and natural history protocol look transferable, and the SMC1A Foundation site states that it has a registry. [ev:rule:R1, ev:seed:org:smc1a-foundation, ev:seed:org:smc1a-foundation:registry]
Outcome measures and endpoints also look transferable, but age of onset and severity still need review before any instrument is adopted. [ev:rule:R2, ev:seed:org:smc1a-foundation]
Clinical network contacts, sites, and investigators may also be useful to share. [ev:rule:R3, ev:seed:org:smc1a-foundation]

A patient organization was not found for ARX in the sources searched, while an SMC1A organization listing was found for the SMC1A Foundation. [ev:seed:org:smc1a-foundation, ev:seed:org:smc1a-foundation:registry]
The SMC1A organization listing passed only an automated check of its own site, and no human has verified it yet. [ev:rule:R3, ev:seed:org:smc1a-foundation]
For ARX, one active NIH-funded research project was found in FY2025-2026, and no SMC1A project was found in NIH RePORTER for FY2025-2026. [ev:reporter:U01DA054170]
We must not assume that a therapeutic strategy is shared just because the two conditions are on the same road. [ev:rule:R4, ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:hpoa:OMIM:300215, ev:g2p:G2P02415, ev:hpoa:OMIM:301044]
The reason is that mechanism is recorded at the gene-and-disease level, not for each family, and our own ARX variant may behave differently. [ev:rule:R4, ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:hpoa:OMIM:300215]

Our family's variant class should be confirmed by a clinical geneticist before anyone acts on loss of function as the right model for that child. [ev:rule:R4, ev:rule:R5, ev:rule:R6, ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:hpoa:OMIM:300215]
We also must not assume that an SMC1A disease model can stand in for ARX, because gene-specific animal or cell models are not interchangeable. [ev:rule:R5, ev:pubmed:models:SMC1A]
Trial design ideas may be worth reviewing, but enrolment in any neighbor trial is not asserted here and must be asked directly with the study team. [ev:rule:R6, ev:rule:R7]

Does the overlap between ARX and SMC1A go beyond common features such as seizures and developmental delay, in your clinical experience? [ev:rule:simgic, ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:hpoa:OMIM:300215, ev:g2p:G2P02415, ev:hpoa:OMIM:301044]
Is the patient organization listed for SMC1A the right contact, and does it run a registry? [ev:seed:org:smc1a-foundation, ev:seed:org:smc1a-foundation:registry]

Has our child's specific ARX variant been functionally classified as loss of function, gain of function, or dominant negative, and does it match the mechanism recorded for the condition? [ev:rule:R4, ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:hpoa:OMIM:300215]
Because the curated ARX mechanism is inferred from variant types rather than direct functional studies, what functional evidence exists for ARX? [ev:rule:R4, ev:g2p:G2P00062, ev:hpoa:OMIM:300215]

glossary.meaning: A change that reduces how much working protein the gene makes, or stops it working.
The main biological way a gene change is thought to cause disease.
A study that follows people over time to learn how a condition changes.
An outcome a study measures, such as seizures, skills, or daily function.
A change in a gene's DNA sequence.
A doctor with specialist training in genetic conditions and test results.
